To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TH gene expression is increased by reserpine in LC and A2 neurons but not in A1 neurons.

1) TH mRNA levels are elevated 2- to-3 fold in noradrenergic A1 and LC cells 24 h following reserpine treatment; 2) TH mRNA levels in these same noradrenergine neurons do not differ significantly 72 h after the reserpine treatment.
reserpine increases levels of TH mRNA in LC and medullary catecholaminergic neurons and that these changes in message levels occur in a region-specific manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of resperine on TH mRNA levels and catecholamine synthesis.
the effects of reserpinization on TH mRNA levels in noradrenergic and adrenergic neurons of the brain stem and the relationship of these changes in gene expression to the depletion of catecholamines.
the mechanisms regulating the expression of the TH gene in noradrenergic and adrenergic neurons of the brainstem and adrenal medulla.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in TH gene expression after reserpine in A1, LC and adrenal medulla and SCG neurons occurs rapidly and is a consequence of the reserpine-induced loss of norepinepherine.
reserpine-induced increases in TH mRNA levels are observed in A1 and A1 and LC noradrenergic cells.
reserpine treatment results in a significant increase in TH mRNA in A1, but not A2, neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of reserine on TH gene expression in LC and A2 neurons is different.
TH mRNA levels are increased in noradrenergic cells after reserpine-induced catecholamine depletion, but not in DA cells.
TH gene expression in LC and A2 neurons increases following NE depletion and that this occurs in A1 neurons as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reserpine treatment increases TH gene expression in LC and A2 but not A1 neurons.

TH gene expression in noradrenergic and epinephrinergic neurons is not the same and that this difference is reflected in the time course and magnitude of TH mRNA increases after depletion of NE stores by reserpine.
TH gene expression in the locus coeruleus increases rapidly and significantly after NE depletion and this is accompanied by an increase in TH activity.
